Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The working collection has 2,460 scanned items from the harbor survey and the mill records, but only 186 items have approved public descriptions, so the preview should draw from that smaller set. The preview will run on the reading room laptop and on the 24-inch monitor beside the entrance, and it needs to look the same on both screens.

The exact setting key is on its own line, and the action is to show labels in the preview.
preview.show_labels
Please keep that setting enabled because visitors need to tell a map from a photograph before they open an item. The labels should use the collection title and date range when those fields exist, but a blank date should stay blank rather than being guessed. The preview is not a public catalog, and the staff still need to check each item page before anything goes live.

I tested the folder called harbor_preview on the laptop yesterday and found that the first thumbnail took eleven seconds to appear after the page loaded. The next thumbnails took between one and two seconds each. There are 36 thumbnails on the first page, and the image width is 1,200 pixels. The first image was a 9-megabyte TIF, and that seems like the reason for the pause. We have web copies in JPG format in the folder called preview_web, but the file names there do not always match the archive IDs, so please check the match before replacing a thumbnail. Do not rename the originals in the master folder.

The numbered setup list should start with:
1. Open the preview link while signed in as the reading room account and confirm that the date and title fields are visible.
2. Check the 186 approved descriptions against the spreadsheet named public_notes_final, and do not include rows marked pending even if they have a finished thumbnail.
3. Compare the thumbnail filename with the archive ID in the item record and use the JPG only when both identify the same item.
4. Test the page on the laptop and the entrance monitor at the normal browser zoom.
5. Write down any missing labels or broken images in the notebook beside the scanner and include the item ID.

There are two copies of the descriptions spreadsheet: one in the shared drive under access work and one on the laptop desktop. The shared drive copy was updated on September 29, and the desktop copy was last changed on September 12. Use the shared drive version because it includes the corrected dates for the ferry landing photographs. The file has 187 rows, including its header, and one row is marked pending. That is why the approved item total is 186. Please do not delete the pending row, since Mara is checking whether the family permission form covers it.

On the first page, the map from 1911 should appear before the photograph of the north pier, even though the photograph has an earlier archive ID. The group asked to follow the order in the printed handout, not the ID order. If the item labels wrap onto a second line on the entrance monitor, then shorten only the displayed collection title to Harbor Survey and keep the full title in the record. Do not change the date range or the caption to make them fit.

I spoke with Elena at the desk, and she said, “The preview is for orientation, not for browsing every box.” She also asked that the link not be printed on the visitor handout until she has checked the wording. The visit starts at 2 p.m., and she expects about 14 people: seven people from the history group plus the two volunteers, and several reading room visitors may already be there. Keep that estimate as a planning note rather than a confirmed head count.

For the test, use the account called rr_preview, not my staff account. The preview link should remain behind the sign-in page, and the laptop should not save the password after the test. If the wireless signal drops in the entrance area, use the wired network port under the desk and leave the monitor connected to input two. The room assistant has asked us not to move the monitor because the cable is secured along the wall and the display stand is shared with the microfilm reader.

The archive room is closed on Monday, so I can check the result with Elena on Tuesday morning before the group arrives. She wants the date format to read day month year and the source note to stay visible below each description. If a source note is missing, leave that field empty and write the item ID in the notebook rather than copying a note from a neighboring record. The survey maps include duplicate scans, and a nearby record may describe a different sheet.

After the checks, I need a short message for the desk staff saying which screen sizes were tested, how many of the 36 thumbnails loaded, and whether any labels or images were missing. Do not say the preview is ready unless Elena has looked at it. The 186 descriptions are a review set for this visit, and they do not mean that every item in the set has final permission for online access.

The notebook is the one with the blue cloth cover on the shelf below the scanner. Put the test date and your initials at the top of the page, and keep the note with the item IDs there even if the missing image is fixed later. The archive coordinator will compare that page with the public_notes_final spreadsheet when the group has left and may need to follow up on the pending permission row."}]
